h: The Wondrous Power of Speech to Create Holiness

p: אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַפְלִיא וְגוֹ׳
"A man or a woman who sets himself apart," etc. (Bamidbar 6:2).
is because the matter of nezirus
is in essence a wondrous thing,
and from what comes from the vine;
גַּם אִם יִשְׁמוֹר אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ
even if a person guards himself
if he does not accept it upon himself
he will not be called holy
that he brings forth from his mouth,
אָז נִקְרָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה קָדוֹשׁ
then he is called holy through it,
And this is truly a great wonder,
And furthermore, such an utterance has the power
when one says "I am hereby a nazir forever,"
and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 10a):
עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא
was called by the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He."
a thing deeper and more wondrous still:
can impose nezirus upon his son
so that through the father's utterance
even though he himself did not perform
And therefore the angel of Shimshon is called
which they said in the Midrash on this parshah
that it is like the matter
of which the verse says "ki yafli";
also on account of his deeds,
for until then he appeared to their eyes
like a man in all his ways,
and in one moment he was transformed
and ascended in the flame to the heavens.
And likewise it is a wonder,
that until now he was a simple man,
And as it says in the Gemara (Nedarim 9b)
that he ate the guilt offering of one nazir
because it was with a proper intention,
And this is the aspect of the power of penitents,
as it says in the holy Zohar
in one day, in one moment,
קְרִיבִין לְגַבֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
they draw near to the Holy One, blessed be He," etc.
that for this reason there was placed
after the parshah of the nazir
because there was revealed to us
that a person's speech is so effective
לִהְיוֹת נִתְהַפֵּךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה כְּרֶגַע
that through it he is transformed in a moment
in the holy Torah to the Kohanim
and through the speech of their mouths
they bring about the flow of the blessings
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר זֶה (בְּמִדְבַּר ו, כז)
